verdict: Lead volume fell sharply this week; several planned channels are still not live.
narrative: Over the last 28 days you received 105 leads at an average cost of $5.56 per lead, but the final week saw a steep pullback — leads dropped 71% and spend fell 56% compared to the prior week, driven by a confirmed three-day period (September 23–25) where ad spend went to zero on your sole active campaign. Cost per lead rose 53% in that same seven-day window as a result. The deeper issue is that Google Search, Local Service Ads, reactivation nurture sequences, and additional Meta audience lanes — all planned to be live by July 31 or August 31 — have not yet launched, leaving one Meta campaign to carry the entire paid load. Restoring continuous spend on the active campaign and accelerating the overdue channel launches are both in motion now, with the goal of distributing lead volume across multiple sources before the next reporting period.

highlights.phrase: leads received in the last 28 days, all from Meta
drop in leads this past week versus the week before
planned program deliverables still not yet live

watch_item.issue: A three-day spend blackout September 23–25 collapsed weekly lead volume and pushed cost per lead up 53%.
watch_item.fix: Continuous spend on the active campaign has been restored and budget pacing is being monitored daily to prevent a repeat gap.
